entities.summary: Prince Dimitri Ivanovich Dolgorukov was a Russian career diplomat born into one of the most prominent families in Russia. Born into nobility, he pursued a career in the service of the Russian Empire, serving as a diplomat and representative in various European courts. In 1855, he was appointed as the Russian Ambassador to the United Kingdom, a position he held until 1862. During his tenure, he played a crucial role in negotiating the Treaty of Paris, which led to the establishment of diplomatic relations between Russia and the United Kingdom. Dolgorukov's diplomatic efforts also contributed to the strengthening of Russia's position in Europe, paving the way for the country's emergence as a major power in the 19th century. His legacy in the world of diplomacy is marked by his skillful navigation of complex international relations and his commitment to promoting Russian interests abroad.
